docs.task: How an explore execution's submit, including `not_covered`, reaches the session detail API.

areas: ostra-core (submit schemas, API DTOs, doc check)
asks: Explain how an explore execution's submit, including `not_covered`, reaches the session detail API.

data_flow.step: The agent calls `submit_explore` with an `ExploreSubmit`-shaped JSON object. The schema it sees comes from `submit_schema(AgentName::Explore)`, derived from the struct with `schemars`. `not_covered` is `#[serde(default)]`, so omitting it parses as an empty list.

Native executor: `run_tools` coerces JSON-string arguments against the schema, then `submit` runs the policy check, `validate_submit`, `doc::check_submit`, and the report-file check. On success `TurnEnd::Submitted { submit: input.clone(), status }` ends the loop and the executor builds `ExecutionResult::with_status(status)` with `r.submit = Some(submit)`.

Harness executor (Claude Code and others): the MCP stdio shim's `call_tool` coerces, validates with `validate_submit` and `doc::check_submit`, and `live.record_submit(args)` stores it in `LiveState.submit`. When the run ends with `End::Submitted`, `outcome::result` returns `ExecutionResult { status: status_of(&submit), submit: Some(submit), .. }`.

`doc::check_submit` for the Explore agent reads the research document at `research_path` and blocks on document errors. It does not compare `not_covered` with the document. The two `not_covered` lists are separate fields that the agent is told to keep equal in `assets/agents/explore/prompt.md`.

The runner awaits `executor.run(...)`, adds the carried-over usage, maps a cancel to `Interrupted` when an interrupt reason is set, and writes the result to the `executions` row with `db.finish_execution` (columns `submit` as JSON text, `final_text`).

Then it appends `SessionEvent::ExecutionFinished { id, result }`. `Inner::append` stores the event (`db.append_event`), runs `materialize`, calls `SessionState::apply`, updates the session row from `view::summary`, broadcasts the stored event, and wakes the driver. `materialize` has no `ExecutionFinished` arm, so the event log and the `executions` row are the only two persisted copies of the submit.

The fold: `apply` stores `result` on the `ExecRecord`, then `on_finished` for `ExecPurpose::Explore { task }` parses `result.submit` into `ExploreSubmit` and sets `ExploreTask.result = Some(sub)` when the status is `Ok` and the parse succeeds. On a parse failure or non-Ok status it retries (up to `ERROR_RETRIES`) or sets `failed`. After a restart the same state comes from `Inner::load`, which folds `db.events(id)`.

Uses of the folded `not_covered` inside the engine: the planner's `explore_complete` (Rule D2) emits `Step::Judge { Sufficiency, subject }` for tasks with non-empty `not_covered` and `judged == false`; `judge_input` writes the `Not covered:` bullet list into the judge's input and returns the summary `"{n} Not covered items across {m} research documents"`; the runner appends `DecisionMade { input_summary, output, reason, .. }`; `coord.rs` appends `Not covered: a; b` to a helper's reply text.
Request: `GET /api/sessions/{id}` goes through the `guard` layer and `get_session`, which finds the workspace for the session and returns `Json(w.engine.detail(&sid)?)`.

`Engine::detail` clones the folded `SessionState` and calls `view::detail(&st, &db, &workspace_id, live_executions)`. `view::detail` loads `ExecutionView`s with `db.list_executions` (which excludes `submit` and `final_text`), decorates them, and builds `stages(s)`, `artifacts(s)`, `phases(s)`, `gates`, `decisions`, `fact_checks(s)`, and the rest of `SessionDetail`.

What of the explore submit reaches `SessionDetail`: (1) `stages`: an Explore card per task with `status` Done when `result` is set and `detail = "{sources_retrieved} sources, {open_questions} open questions"`, plus `project`, `executions` and `gate`. (2) `artifacts`: an `ArtifactRef { kind: "research", label: "Research: ...", path: research_path, project }` from `r.research_path`. (3) `decisions`: for a Sufficiency decision, `input_summary` carries only the count of Not covered items and the number of documents; `output` and `reason` are the judge's own. (4) `executions`: status, usage, error, but no `submit`. `scope_covered`, `findings_summary` and the `not_covered` strings are not in the response.

Other routes that do expose the raw submit: `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events` returns `StoredEvent`s, including `execution_finished` with `result.submit` (so `not_covered` is present there), and the same events are broadcast over the WebSocket as they are appended. The web client handles `execution_finished` in `web/src/lib/events.ts` and reloads the session detail on it (`useExecution.ts`). `GET /api/executions/{id}` returns only an `ExecutionView`, and `WorkspaceDb::execution_output` has no caller in `ostra-server`.

document.problem: An explore agent ends by calling `submit_explore`, whose payload `ExploreSubmit` carries `not_covered: Vec<String>`. The engine reads that payload into fold state and the planner/judge use it, but `SessionDetail` has no field that carries the submit. The Explore stage card in `SessionDetail.stages` keeps only `sources_retrieved` and `open_questions` from it, so the `not_covered` strings do not appear in the session detail response today. Only a count of them appears, inside the Sufficiency decision's `input_summary`.

submit.findings_summary: Both executors validate the explore submit with `validate_submit` and `doc::check_submit`, and return it as the untyped `ExecutionResult.submit`. The runner stores it in the `executions` row and in an `ExecutionFinished` event. The fold (`state.rs::on_finished`) parses it into `ExploreTask.result: Option<ExploreSubmit>`, and the planner (Rule D2) and `judge_input.rs` read `not_covered` from there. `view::detail` builds `SessionDetail` from that fold, but the response carries no field for the submit: `ExecutionView` omits `submit`, and the Explore `StageCard.detail` is only "N sources, M open questions". The `not_covered` strings reach clients only through the raw `execution_finished` event (`/api/sessions/{id}/events` and the WebSocket), and as a count inside the Sufficiency `DecisionView.input_summary`.

docs.task: How the console renders a research run card on the session board.

areas: web (session board, mobile session, artifact research view)
asks: How the console renders a research run card on the session board.

data_flow.step: The explore agent ends by calling submit_explore with research_path, scope_covered, findings_summary, sources_retrieved, open_questions, and not_covered.

When the execution finishes with status Ok and a parseable submit, the fold stores the whole payload on the task. A failure with retries left clears exec; otherwise it sets failed. An execution-failed gate later sets t.gate.

The planner reads not_covered from the stored result. Finished tasks whose items are unjudged make Step::Judge Sufficiency (Rule D2) until SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS is reached; the fold sets judged and increments sufficiency_rounds when the decision applies.

view::stages maps each ExploreTask to one StageCard of kind explore. Status precedence is result, abandoned, failed, running, else pending. Label is 'Research: ' plus the first line of the task, cut to 120 characters. detail is 'N sources, M open questions' only when a result exists. not_covered, scope_covered, and findings_summary are not copied onto the card. A Sufficiency card 'Check research coverage' with detail 'N rounds' follows when any Sufficiency decision exists.
The same view layer lists the research document as an ArtifactRef of kind research with label 'Research: <task>' and the project, once a result exists.

The card list travels in SessionDetail.stages (TypeScript type web/src/api/gen/StageCard.ts). SessionScreen loads it with api.session(id) and reloads on a throttled 400 ms refresh for every live session event.

laneStates folds the cards of the Research lane into one stepper entry: waiting beats running beats failed or blocked; all done gives done with the last done card's detail; some done gives 'k of n done'. defaultLane picks the lane of the current gate, else the first waiting or current lane.
LanePanel keeps cards whose lane equals the selected lane and renders each as a StageRow with label, status, and stageMeta. Clicking toggles the detail box (see pattern).

StageRow draws the dot and label (CSS ellipsis, one line) and the meta in mono 2xs muted text. Mobile draws the same fields in LaneCard, and a tap goes to stageTarget: the gate if waiting, else the running or latest execution.

The Not covered list is shown in full only in the research document view, opened from the sidebar or mobile artifact list, not from the board card: the Overview 'Not covered' stat and the 'Not covered' chapter with the attention flag.

document.title: Research run card on the session board

submit.findings_summary: The board has no dedicated research card component. ostra-engine view.rs::stages emits one StageCard (stage explore) per ExploreTask, with label 'Research: <first line of task>', a status mapped from result, abandoned, failed, and running, and a detail 'N sources, M open questions' only once a result exists. The web LanePanel draws it as a design StageRow, whose meta comes from stageMeta (live execution summary while running, otherwise detail plus project). A selected card shows static Produces and Protects text, the detail, execution buttons, and a Go to the gate button. The mobile LaneCard draws the same fields. ExploreSubmit.not_covered is never copied onto the card. The planner (Rule D2) and Sufficiency judge consume it, and the console shows it only in the research document view.
not_covered: The sidebar session tree (TreeRun in view.rs, web/src/shell/Sidebar.tsx) and how it labels explore runs.
The execution screen for an explore run and the GateCard rendering of the execution-failed gate that a failed research card links to.
The Decisions tab rendering of the Sufficiency decision (web/src/screens/session/SidePanels.tsx).
Browser tests and docs pages that describe the board were only grepped for mentions, not read in full.
The design-sync target (.design-sync/NOTES.md) that applies if web/ or design/ change.
submit.scope_covered: How a research run is turned into a StageCard by the engine and drawn on the desktop and mobile session board, including where its Not covered data does and does not appear; the sidebar run tree, execution screen, and Decisions tab were left out.
